summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Singapore documents (GIP factsheets 2009-2025, EDB web page and GIP-select release, parliamentary answers and statements). The factsheets carry rules, not statistics: this pass adds eligibility thresholds, renewal conditions, deadlines and processing times by version. Parliamentary answers add the GIP fund deployment figures (Oct 2022), EDB's exact jobs count, and MAS family-office tax-incentive context.

observations.quote: It will take approximately 9-12 months for a GIP Application to be processed.
observations.notes: Approximate time EDB gives in the factsheet dated 16 Aug 2021, subject to a complete submission and due diligence checks.

observations.quote: It will take approximately 12 months for a GIP Application to be processed.
observations.notes: Approximate time EDB gives in the factsheet updated 2 Aug 2023, subject to a complete submission and due diligence checks.

observations.quote: It will take approximately 12 months for a GIP Application to be processed.
observations.notes: Approximate time EDB gives in the factsheet updated 5 May 2025, subject to a complete submission and due diligence checks.

observations.quote: Between 2011 and 2022, GIP investors created 24,699 jobs across a range of roles
observations.notes: EDB's exact count; ministers rounded it to 'more than 24,000' (sgp-parl-oa-gip-2023) and 'over 24,000' (sgp-parl-cos-mti-2023). Whether limited to direct-investment (Option A) investors is not stated here.

observations.quote: The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) has appointed seven fund management companies as Global Investor Programme (GIP)-select funds.
observations.notes: GIP-select fund managers appointed under the new Option B (S$25 million), for three years from 12 May 2023; listed in para 4. Recorded under the indicator for approved investment-pooling entities; unit is fund management companies.

observations.location: Minister for Trade and Industry, GIP passage
observations.quote: Over the past 11 years, GIP investors have brought in around $5.5 billion in total business expenditure, generating over 24,000 jobs in Singapore.
observations.notes: 'Over 24,000' jobs over 'the past 11 years' as of 28 Feb 2023; period label follows the S$5.5 billion row from the same sentence (o-020736da23) and is approximate. EDB's exact figure for 2011-2022 is 24,699 (sgp-edb-gipselect-mr-2023).

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng
observations.quote: Of this S$1.62 billion, the fund managers have deployed 87.2% and this translates to S$1.41 billion into actual investments.
observations.notes: Part of the S$1.62 billion GIP investors had put into approved GIP funds as of Oct 2022 (o-d02ecc9baa) that fund managers had invested. Start date not stated; period label follows that row.

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng
observations.quote: Of this S$1.62 billion, the fund managers have deployed 87.2% and this translates to S$1.41 billion into actual investments.
observations.notes: Share of the S$1.62 billion in GIP funds that had been deployed into investments as of Oct 2022.

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng
observations.quote: 65.6% of this S$1.41 billion, which is S$930 million, has been invested in Singapore-based companies.
observations.notes: Part of the S$1.41 billion deployed by GIP funds that went into Singapore-based companies, as of Oct 2022.

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng
observations.quote: 65.6% of this S$1.41 billion, which is S$930 million, has been invested in Singapore-based companies.
observations.notes: Share of the S$1.41 billion deployed by GIP funds (not of the S$1.62 billion) invested in Singapore-based companies, as of Oct 2022.

observations.location: reply to Mr Pritam Singh's second supplementary question
observations.quote: GIP investors who are approved as PRs are much lesser than 1% of the total number of PRs approved each year.
observations.notes: Spoken as 'much lesser than 1%' of all PRs approved each year; recorded as a range of 0 to 1 per the dataset's 'fewer than N' rule. The years covered are not stated (the exchange concerned 2020-2022); period set to the dataset's convention for unspecified periods. Main applicants only, as far as stated ('GIP investors').

observations.location: oral answer, paragraph beginning 'Based on available data'
observations.quote: Based on available data over the past three years, about 3% out of 1,300 applications were rejected.
observations.notes: Applications for MAS tax incentives for single family office funds (sections 13O/13U), not GIP residence applications; context only, like sfo_tax_incentive_recipients. 'Over the past three years' to 5 Nov 2025; exact period not given, so the dataset's convention for unspecified periods is used.

observations.location: oral answer, paragraph beginning 'Based on available data'
observations.quote: Based on available data over the past three years, about 3% out of 1,300 applications were rejected.
observations.notes: 'About 3%' of the 1,300 SFO tax-incentive applications over the past three years were rejected; others withdrew before applying formally. MAS tax incentives, not the GIP; context only.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's company turnover, in the most recent year and on average over the last 3 years (applicants with an entrepreneurial and business track record)
program_terms.quote: At least S$10 million per annum in the most recent year; and
program_terms.notes: Factsheet 'Updated as of 1 June 2009' (PDF p. 8). Also 'At least S$10 million per annum on average for the last 3 years'. Businesses may be consolidated to meet the minimum; share ownership, role and profitability are considered. Start and end dates not given: the 1 Oct 2010 factsheet shows S$30 million (sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2010).

program_terms.applies_to: minimum entrepreneurial (and business) track record of the applicant, with audited financial statements for the last 3 years
program_terms.quote: You must possess at least 3 years of entrepreneurial track record
program_terms.notes: Same 3-year requirement in the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2014 factsheets and for Established Business Owners in the 2021, 2023 and 2025 factsheets. Family Office Principals need 5 years from the 2021 factsheet (separate row).

program_terms.applies_to: turnover of the company employing an applicant who is a senior corporate manager without an entrepreneurial track record (Option A only; at least 10 years of corporate management experience)
program_terms.quote: The turnover of the company in which you are employed must be at least S$100 million.
program_terms.notes: Senior managers had to have 'at least 10 years of corporate management experience', hold a role such as Chairman, CEO, CFO or CTO and choose Option A. Same in the Oct 2010 and Apr 2011 factsheets; the route is absent from the Oct 2012 factsheet. Dates of introduction and removal not found.

program_terms.applies_to: time to make the investment after Approval-in-Principle of PR (the AIP is valid for 6 months)
program_terms.quote: You will be required to make your investment within the 6 months' period.
program_terms.notes: AIP issued by ICA 'which is valid for 6 months'. The same 6-month deadline is in every factsheet read (2010, 2011, 2012, 2014, 2021, 2023, 2025). Under the 2009-2010 options the money had to come from the applicant's personal bank account in Singapore. For business investments, audited financial statements were due at the end of the 2nd and 4th year (2nd, 3rd and 4th year in the 2012 and 2014 factsheets).

program_terms.applies_to: Long Term Visit Pass for family members who cannot be included for PR (unmarried children aged 21 and above; from 2011 also parents), tied to the main applicant's re-entry permit
program_terms.quote: Unmarried children who are 21 years and above of age are eligible to apply for the 5-year Long Term Visit Pass (LTVP)
program_terms.notes: Renewable and tied to the validity of the re-entry permit. The 5-year LTVP is also in the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2014 factsheets (parents added from 1 Jan 2011); the 2021-2025 factsheets give no duration, only that it is tied to the re-entry permit.

program_terms.applies_to: children included as dependants in the PR application must be below this age (unmarried, as at the date of application, in the 2014 and later factsheets)
program_terms.quote: Your spouse and children (below 21 years old) are eligible to apply for PR under your PR application.
program_terms.notes: Same limit in all later factsheets read (2010-2025). Male dependants are liable for National Service.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's company turnover, in the most recent year and on average over the last 3 years (applicants with an entrepreneurial and business track record)
program_terms.quote: At least S$30 million per annum in the most recent year; and
program_terms.notes: Factsheet 'Updated as of 1 October 2010'; also in the 1 April 2011 factsheet (sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2011, PDF p. 2). Up from S$10 million in the June 2009 factsheet; the date of change is not given. Replaced by S$50 million (S$200 million for real estate and construction) by the Oct 2012 factsheet.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's company turnover in the most recent year and on average over the last 3 years, if the company is in the real estate or construction-related industry
program_terms.quote: your company's turnover must be at least S$200 million in the most recent year
program_terms.notes: Factsheet 'Updated as of 2 October 2012'. Not in the 2014 factsheet, which limits qualifying companies to the industries in its Annex A (real estate and construction are not listed). Start date not given.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's company turnover in the most recent year and on average over the last 3 years, companies in sectors other than real estate and construction
program_terms.quote: your company's turnover must be at least S$50 million in the most recent year, and at least S$50 million per annum on average for the last 3 years.
program_terms.notes: Same S$50 million in the April 2014 factsheet (sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2014, PDF p. 2), which adds that the company must only be engaged in the industries in Annex A. Replaced by S$200 million for Established Business Owners (sgp-edb-gip-factsheet-2021). Start date not given.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's minimum shareholding in the qualifying company, if privately owned
program_terms.quote: If your company is privately-owned, you should have at least 30% shareholding in the company.
program_terms.notes: Same in the 2014 factsheet and, for Established Business Owners, in the 2021, 2023 and 2025 factsheets (if publicly listed: one of the largest individual shareholders). Next Generation Business Owners: immediate family at least 30% or the largest shareholder.

program_terms.applies_to: Option A: milestones of the 3-year business or investment plan must be met within this period from the date of investment
program_terms.quote: You are required to fulfill the milestones outlined in your business or investment plan 3 years from the date of investment.
program_terms.notes: Option A applicants had to submit 'a detailed 3-year business or investment plan'. Became 5 years in the 2014 factsheet.

program_terms.applies_to: first re-entry permit issued on formalisation of PR; renewed for 3 or 5 years if conditions are met
program_terms.quote: Upon the formalisation of your PR status, you will be issued a Re-Entry Permit (REP) for 5 years.
program_terms.notes: Same 5-year REP in the 2014, 2021, 2023 and 2025 factsheets. 3-year renewal: investment conditions plus either the business condition or residence by the applicant or one GIP-PR dependant for more than half of the time; 5-year renewal: investment conditions, the business condition and residence by the applicant and dependants for more than half of the time.

program_terms.applies_to: re-entry permit renewal: business set up in Singapore must have at least this many Singaporean employees (with the total business spending condition)
program_terms.quote: You have set up a business in Singapore with 5 or more Singaporean employees and have incurred at least S$1 million in total business spending a year
program_terms.notes: Required for a 5-year renewal; for a 3-year renewal this or the residence condition. Same in the 2014 factsheet ('total business expenditure'). Start and end dates not given; the 2021 factsheet requires 10 employees with at least 5 Singapore Citizens.

program_terms.applies_to: re-entry permit renewal: total business spending a year by the business set up in Singapore
program_terms.quote: have incurred at least S$1 million in total business spending a year
program_terms.notes: With 5 or more Singaporean employees. Same in the April 2014 factsheet. S$2 million a year in the 2021 factsheet. Dates not given.

program_terms.applies_to: time to formalise PR status after making the investment
program_terms.quote: You are required to formalize your PR status within 12 months from the date of your investment.
program_terms.notes: Same in the 2014 factsheet. From the 2021 factsheet the 12 months run from the date of Final Approval (separate row).

program_terms.applies_to: maximum time between paying the application fee and submitting the application
program_terms.quote: The time between the remittance of the application fee and the submission of application form must be within 1 month.
program_terms.notes: 2014 factsheet: '1 month or less'; 2021, 2023 and 2025 factsheets: supporting documents must reach EDB within 1 month of the fee remittance.

program_terms.applies_to: Option A: milestones of the 5-year business or investment plan must be met within this period from the date of investment
program_terms.quote: You are required to fulfill the milestones outlined in your business or investment plan within 5 years of the date of investment.
program_terms.notes: Factsheet 'Updated as of 1 April 2014' (PDF p. 9). Up from 3 years in the 2012 factsheet. The 2021-2025 factsheets also require a 5-year plan for Options A and C.

program_terms.applies_to: Established Business Owners: annual turnover of the company the applicant runs, in the year before applying and on average over the three years before
program_terms.quote: You should currently be running a company 1 with an annual turnover of at least S$200 million in the year immediately preceding your application
program_terms.notes: Plus at least 3 years of track record, 30% shareholding if privately held, and an Annex B industry; up to 2 businesses may be consolidated. Same in the 2023 and 2025 factsheets. Probably from the March 2020 revision (see event e-79264ab0fa), but the factsheet gives no start date.

program_terms.applies_to: Next Generation Business Owners: annual turnover of the family company, in the year before applying and on average over the three years before
program_terms.quote: This company's annual turnover must be at least S$500 million in the year immediately preceding your application
program_terms.notes: Immediate family must hold at least 30% or be the largest shareholder; applicant must be in the management team; Annex B industry. Same in the 2023 and 2025 factsheets. Start date not given.

program_terms.applies_to: Founders of Fast Growth Companies: valuation of the company the applicant founded and is one of the largest individual shareholders of
program_terms.quote: You must be a founder and one of the largest individual shareholders of a company with a valuation of at least S$500 million
program_terms.notes: The company must have been invested into by reputable venture capital or private equity firms and be in an Annex B industry. The 2023 and 2025 factsheets specify 'a non-publicly listed company'. Start date not given.

program_terms.applies_to: Family Office Principals: net investible assets of the applicant (financial assets, excluding real estate); qualifies for Option C only
program_terms.quote: You must have net investible assets of at least S$200 million.
program_terms.notes: Also at least 5 years of entrepreneurial, investment or management track record. Same in the 2023 and 2025 factsheets (which add that Contact Singapore may judge the suitability of the assets). Net investible assets must be certified by an accredited audit firm or a Singapore bank, law firm or trust company (Annex A, item D2).

program_terms.applies_to: Family Office Principals: minimum entrepreneurial, investment or management track record
program_terms.quote: You must possess at least 5 years of entrepreneurial, investment or management track record
program_terms.notes: Same in the 2023 and 2025 factsheets. Other profiles: 3 years (Established Business Owners).

program_terms.applies_to: Option A: applicant's minimum shareholding in the Option A company, and must be in its management team
program_terms.quote: You should have at least 30% shareholding in the Option A company
program_terms.notes: Same in the 2023 and 2025 factsheets (2023: ordinary shares only; 2025: if invested through a listed qualifying company, one of its largest individual shareholders). Company must be in an Annex B industry; a 5-year business plan is assessed.

program_terms.applies_to: re-entry permit renewal: employees of the Option A company, the business set up (Option B) or the family office (Option C), of whom at least 5 Singapore Citizens
program_terms.quote: Your Option A 9 company in Singapore must employ at least 10 employees with at least 5 Singapore Citizens, and incurs an annual total business expenditure of at least S$2 million
program_terms.notes: Option C: also 3 professionals (non-family members in legal, tax or investment roles). Only incremental jobs and spending from the investment date count for existing companies. Required for a 5-year renewal; for a 3-year renewal this or residence of the applicant or all GIP dependants for more than half of the time. Replaced from 15 Mar 2023 (sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023).

program_terms.applies_to: re-entry permit renewal: annual total business expenditure of the Option A company, the business set up (Option B) or the family office (Option C)
program_terms.quote: incurs an annual total business expenditure of at least S$2 million
program_terms.notes: With at least 10 employees (5 Singapore Citizens). The 2023 annex to sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023 words the old rule as S$2 million by Year 5 (t-6fa791f371). Not in the 2023 factsheet.

program_terms.applies_to: time to formalise PR status after the Final Approval letter
program_terms.quote: You are required to formalise your PR status within 12 months from the date of Final Approval.
program_terms.notes: Same in the 2023 and 2025 factsheets. Earlier factsheets counted 12 months from the date of investment.

program_terms.applies_to: Option A re-entry permit renewal: employees of the Option A company, at least half Singapore Citizens, of whom at least 10 incremental
program_terms.quote: must employ minimally 30 employees (at least half of whom must be Singapore Citizens), out of which there must be at least 10 incremental employees
program_terms.notes: Factsheet updated 2 Aug 2023; valid_from is the date of the new requirements (sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023). Same in the 2025 factsheet (incremental jobs counted from the application date there, from Final Approval in 2023). 5-year renewal also needs residence of the applicant or all GIP dependants for more than half of the time; 3-year renewal one of the two.

program_terms.applies_to: Option B re-entry permit renewal: GIP-select fund investment to be maintained
program_terms.quote: Maintain the S$25 million investment in a GIP-select fund
program_terms.notes: Same in the 2025 factsheet. valid_from from sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023.

program_terms.applies_to: Option C re-entry permit renewal: incremental family office professionals, at least 3 of them Singapore Citizens, plus maintaining S$50 million in the qualifying investments
program_terms.quote: employ at least 5 incremental Family Office professionals 15 (with at least 3 Singapore Citizens)
program_terms.notes: Footnote 15: advisory roles or board appointments in legal, tax, investment or philanthropy. Same in the 2025 factsheet (where the S$50 million must stay in EDB specified investments, i.e. listed equities). valid_from from sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023.

program_terms.applies_to: Option C: time after Final Approval to deploy at least S$50 million in the qualifying investment categories
program_terms.quote: Option C applicants will be required to demonstrate that a minimum of S$50 million has been deployed into the stipulated investment categories no later than 12 months from the date of Final Approval.
program_terms.notes: The S$50 million must first be transferred into Singapore by Approval-in-Principle. Same deadline in the 2025 factsheet. valid_from from sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023.

program_terms.applies_to: the window to apply for re-entry permit renewal opens this long before the permit expires
program_terms.quote: The window to apply opens 3 months before the expiry of your REP.
program_terms.notes: Without a valid REP, PR is lost on leaving Singapore. Same in the 2025 factsheet.

program_terms.applies_to: assets under management of a fund management company to qualify as a GIP-select fund manager
program_terms.quote: Total Assets Under Management (AUM) of at least S$1 billion;
program_terms.notes: Criteria of the call for proposals of 2-31 March 2023 (valid_from = start of the call). Also: fund and manager incorporated and based in Singapore with MAS approval; raised at least three funds; general partner with at least 10 years of investment track record.

program_terms.applies_to: share of GIP monies received from Option B investors that a GIP-select fund must invest in Singapore-based companies in EDB-promoted sectors (or S$50 million, whichever is lower)
program_terms.quote: The GIP-select funds will invest at least 50% of GIP monies received or S$50 million of GIP monies received (whichever is lower)
program_terms.notes: Alternative cap in the fund_singapore_investment_amount row. Sectors listed in Annex B. valid_from = start of the managers' appointment (footnote 3). Before 2023 EDB described the old rule as a fund investing at least 50% in Singapore-based companies (sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023).

program_terms.applies_to: amount of GIP monies a GIP-select fund must invest in Singapore-based companies, if lower than 50% of GIP monies received
program_terms.quote: or S$50 million of GIP monies received (whichever is lower) from GIP Option B investors
program_terms.notes: Whichever is lower of 50% of GIP monies or S$50 million.

program_terms.applies_to: initial appointment of GIP-select fund managers, renewable after review of their local investments
program_terms.quote: The appointment of the GIP-select fund managers will last for three years, starting from 12 May 2023.
program_terms.notes: Managers submit quarterly reports to EDB; EDB may call for proposals for new GIP-select funds every year.

program_terms.applies_to: minimum investment under the GIP, as stated in Parliament on 9 Jan 2018
program_terms.location: supplementary reply to Mr Thomas Chua (second)
program_terms.quote: For example, the minimum investment required under GIP is $2.5 million.
program_terms.notes: Minister of State's statement ('$' = Singapore dollars in context); confirms the S$2.5 million minimum in force 2011 to 14 Mar 2023. She added that it is higher than the minimum in Australia, the US and the UK.

events.title: Call for proposals for GIP-select funds opens
events.description: EDB ran a call for proposals from 2 to 31 March 2023 to appoint fund managers for the new GIP-select funds (Option B, S$25 million); qualifying managers needed at least S$1 billion under management.
events.quote: following an open and transparent Call for Proposal (CFP) exercise conducted from 2 to 31 March 2023

gaps: Effective dates of the eligibility changes between factsheet versions (S$10m to S$30m turnover by Oct 2010; S$50m/S$200m by Oct 2012; profile-based criteria from the 2020 revision) are not printed in the factsheets; rows leave valid_from/valid_to empty where unknown.
No GIP application, approval or rejection counts appear in any factsheet; numbers come only from parliamentary answers.

ledger.contains: Contact Singapore GIP factsheet 'Updated as of 1 June 2009' (8 pp.): three investment options (S$1m business; S$1.5m business or GIP-approved fund; S$2m business or fund with up to 50% in owner-occupied residential property), eligibility (business track record, entrepreneurial background), assessment criteria (3 years' track record, company turnover S$10m in the latest year and on average over 3 years; senior corporate managers: 10 years' experience, company turnover S$100m, Option A only), family provisions (spouse and children under 21 for PR; unmarried children 21+ get a 5-year LTVP; parents and parents-in-law PR at S$300,000 each), application steps (AIP valid 6 months, invest within 6 months from a Singapore personal account, Contact Singapore holds evidence for 5 years, audited statements at end of years 2 and 4, notarised documents valid 1 year), list of 13 approved business sectors, contact details. No statistics. Investment options and parents' price were already recorded; this pass adds turnover, track-record, senior-manager, investment-deadline, LTVP and child-age rules. Document-handling details (custody 5 years, notarisation 1 year) are noted here, not tabulated.

GIP factsheet 'Updated as of 1 October 2010' (8 pp.): same three options as 2009 (S$1m/S$1.5m/S$2m with up to 50% residential property) and an important note that from 1 Jan 2011 the options become S$2.5m in a business or S$2.5m in a GIP-approved fund, the property option ends and parents can no longer be included (5-year LTVP instead); company turnover threshold now S$30m (latest year and 3-year average); senior managers S$100m and 10 years; family, application and sector sections as in 2009. No statistics. The 2011 options and change event were already recorded; this pass adds the S$30m turnover rule (other repeated rules are noted on the 2009 rows).

GIP factsheet 'Updated as of 1 April 2011' (7 pp.): Option A S$2.5m business, Option B S$2.5m GIP-approved fund; turnover S$30m (latest year and 3-year average); senior corporate managers (Option A) 10 years' experience, company turnover S$100m; spouse and children under 21 for PR, parents and children 21+ 5-year LTVP; AIP valid 6 months, invest S$2.5m within 6 months from a sole-name Singapore account; audited statements at end of years 2 and 4; 13 sectors. No statistics and no rule not already recorded from the 2009, 2010 or other factsheets (each rule's row notes that it also appears here).

GIP factsheet 'Updated as of 2 October 2012' (10 pp.): Options A and B at S$2.5m (fund must invest in Singapore-based companies); turnover S$200m for real estate or construction companies, S$50m for other sectors (latest year and 3-year average); 30% shareholding if privately owned; Option A 3-year business plan with milestones within 3 years; family (spouse and children under 21; parents and children 21+ 5-year LTVP); first re-entry permit 5 years and renewal conditions (3-year or 5-year renewal: business with 5+ Singaporean employees and S$1m total business spending a year, and/or residence more than half the time); application fee S$5,650 (bank details), forms within 1 month of fee; AIP 6 months; audited statements at end of years 2, 3 and 4; formalise PR within 12 months of investment; 25 approved industries including family office. No statistics. Fee was already recorded; this pass adds the turnover, shareholding, plan, re-entry permit, renewal, formalisation and fee-to-application deadline rules.

GIP factsheet 'Updated as of 1 April 2014' (9 pp.; the source title says March 2014): Options A and B at S$2.5m; turnover S$50m (year before and 3-year average), company only in Annex A industries; 30% shareholding if privately held; Option A 5-year plan with milestones within 5 years; family rules (unmarried children under 21; parents and children 21+ 5-year LTVP); 5-year re-entry permit and renewal conditions (5 Singaporean employees, S$1m total business expenditure a year, residence more than half the time); application fee S$7,000, forms within 1 month of fee; AIP 6 months; formalise within 12 months of investment; disclaimer; Annex A list of 25 industries (incl. family office and financial services). No statistics. Fee already recorded; this pass adds the 5-year plan rule; the other rules repeat 2012 and are noted on those rows.

EDB GIP factsheet dated 16 August 2021 (16 pp.): four applicant profiles with qualifying criteria (Established Business Owners: 3 years, turnover S$200m, 30% if private; Next Generation Business Owners: family company turnover S$500m; Founders of Fast Growth Companies: company valuation S$500m with VC/PE backing; Family Office Principals: 5 years and S$200m net investible assets, Option C only); Options A, B and C at S$2.5m (C: single family office with AUM S$200m, S$50m held in Singapore); assessment criteria (5-year plans, 30% shareholding in Option A company); 7 processing steps (AIP 6 months; formalise within 12 months of Final Approval); processing time about 9-12 months; post-AIP documents; 5-year re-entry permit and renewal conditions (10 employees incl. 5 citizens, S$2m annual total business expenditure, 3 professionals for Option C; residence more than half the time); application fee S$10,000 and bank details; documents within 1 month; Annex A supporting documents; Annex B industry list. No programme statistics. Option C and fee were already recorded; this pass adds the profile thresholds, Option A shareholding, renewal, formalisation rules and the processing time.

EDB GIP factsheet updated 2 August 2023 (20 pp.): same four profiles and thresholds as 2021 (founders' company must be non-publicly listed); Option A S$10m (paid-up capital counts), Option B S$25m in a GIP-select fund, Option C single family office with AUM S$200m and S$50m transferred by AIP and deployed in 4 categories within 12 months of Final Approval; assessment criteria; processing about 12 months; post-AIP documents per option; formalisation within 12 months; 5-year re-entry permit, renewal window opens 3 months before expiry; renewal conditions (Option A 30 employees, half citizens, 10 incremental; B maintain S$25m; C 5 incremental family office professionals incl. 3 citizens and maintain S$50m; residence more than half the time); fee S$10,000; supporting documents; industries. No statistics. Option amounts, AUM and fee were already recorded (from this and other sources); this pass adds the 2023 renewal conditions, deployment deadline, renewal window and processing time.

EDB GIP factsheet updated 5 May 2025 (19 pp.): same profiles and thresholds as 2023; Options A S$10m, B S$25m, C SFO with AUM S$200m and S$50m in 'EDB specified investments' (only equities listed on Singapore approved exchanges); processing about 12 months; post-AIP documents per option; formalisation 12 months; 5-year re-entry permit, renewal window 3 months; renewal conditions as 2023 (incremental jobs counted from the application date); application fee S$20,000, non-refundable regardless of outcome; documents within 1 month; notarisation within the year before application; Annex A supporting documents; Annex B industries. No statistics. Fee and options already recorded; this pass adds the processing time; the other rules repeat 2021/2023 and are noted on those rows.

EDB GIP web page (last updated 2 Oct 2026): short description of the GIP (PR for investors with business track record, run by Contact Singapore), links to the factsheet and e-application forms (about 30 minutes to complete), Form 4 with the S$100 ICA processing fee per applicant, family-background sheet (about 15 minutes), links to GIP-select funds. Only programme number is the S$100 fee, already recorded; the form-completion times are not programme terms.
